### Staying signed in
A Mac looked after by an organisation no longer signs itself out on its own.
Its session renews quietly in the background, and an error from the server is no longer mistaken for the session ending — a message about one thing you are not allowed to see used to sign you out of everything. If the session really has ended, Kahf Guard now says so and offers to reconnect, instead of quietly showing an organisation's name while enforcing nothing.
### Uninstall protection is yours to decide
Uninstall protection no longer switches itself on when a Mac is set up for a child or an organisation, and whoever uses the Mac can now turn it off again through the usual 24-hour wait. Before, on a managed Mac the setting could be switched on but never off, and tapping it did nothing at all.
Turning it on is unchanged, and so is the wait — the point of the delay is that it cannot be removed in the moment you want to get past it.
### Fixes
Kahf Guard no longer claims to be managed by an organisation while signed out of that organisation.
